subject: BYOK topology & rotation cadence - MedSys private deployment
messages:
From: Rana Singh <rana.singh@medsys.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medsys.com
Date: 2026-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BYOK topology & rotation cadence - MedSys private deployment

Hi David,

Thanks for agreeing to review our BYOK approach for the private deployment we're planning with Redwood. High level constraints:
- Regulated PHI (HIPAA) workload, SOC 2 in progress.
- Private deployment into our VPC (no internet egress from host subnets for HSM).
- Cloud partner will provide HSM appliances (n=3 in active-standby topology) and we need a clear rotation cadence and operator model.

Specific asks for the review:
1) Recommended key wrapping/unwrapping flow when we bring our keys (BYOK) to the HSMs.
2) Suggested rotation schedule that minimizes downtime and meets audit evidence expectations.
3) Network segmentation and egress restrictions that let Redwood telemetry and telemetry-scrubbing reach our SIEM without exposing key material.
4) Example runbook for a rotation ceremony and an emergency key revoke (break-glass).

Attached: MedSys encryption requirements (short). Also attaching a rough topology diagram.

Can your team propose an architecture and a 60-day rollout plan? We're hoping for a 90-minute design workshop next week.

Thanks,
Rana
Security Architect, MedSys Healthcare

From: david.kim@redwood.ai
To: Rana Singh <rana.singh@medsys.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-03T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK topology & rotation cadence - MedSys private deployment

Rana —

Thanks for the clear brief. Looping in Kim (security lead) and Monica (on-prem operations) to map our recommended pattern. Initial thoughts (high level):

- Topology outline:
  * HSM cluster: use your HSM appliances in a quorum-based cluster (prefer >2 with an odd quorum where supported). We recommend keeping the crypto material sealed inside the HSM; no plaintext key leaves the appliance.
  * Redwood KMS proxy sidecars: a small, authenticated sidecar runs in the same subnet as the service nodes. The sidecar performs mTLS-authenticated wrap/unwrap flows to the HSM via an operator-exposed gateway.
  * Wrap-key gateway: a dedicated management subnet with a bastion-managed gateway that performs HSM proxying and attestation checks. Avoid direct internet egress from HSM subnets; outbound telemetry should be proxied through the gateway.

- BYOK flow suggestion:
  1) Customer generates root key material locally (offline).
  2) Root key is imported to the HSM using HSM vendor import tooling — HSM performs attestation and returns an import receipt.
  3) Operational keys for workloads are derived inside the HSM; we prefer a wrap/unwrap model where root keys never leave the HSM unencrypted.
  4) For interactions with Redwood runtime, use an ephemeral key-wrapping token issued by the HSM gateway; sidecars hold short-lived tokens and never materialize long-term keys.

- Rotation cadence and zero-downtime approach:
  * Staged rotation using dual-wrap periods (T0: old+new active) for 48–72 hours depending on workload.
  * Rollout phases: canary (1–2 nodes), staggered per availability zone, then wide.
  * Backward-compatibility: ensure services can accept both wrapped variants during the dual period.
  * Audit evidence: include import receipts, attestation logs, and per-token usage traces in the rotation artifact.

- Networking and telemetry:
  * HSM subnets: deny all internet egress.
  * Gateway subnet: tightly controlled egress to SIEM/Redwood telemetry endpoints over TLS through an approved NAT.
  * Bastion + jumpbox for operator actions; everything over mTLS with client certs.
  * SIEM: ship only telemetry hashes and attestation receipts (no plaintext key data).

- Runbook items we recommend including:
  * Pre-rotation checklist (backups, import receipts, quorum check, scheduled windows).
  * Operator separation matrix (who can request, who can approve, who can execute).
  * Rollback procedure and smoke tests (token issuance, sample decrypts, health-check endpoints).
  * Emergency revoke: fail closed by updating routing to a quarantine key policy and notifying the SRE pager.

Next steps: Kim and Monica — can you add ops/security-specific constraints (split custody, quorum enforcement, evidence collection formats) and a proposed 60-day plan? Rana — we can run the 90-minute workshop on 2026-04-07 or 2026-04-09; tell us which works.

Best,
David
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, Rana Singh <rana.singh@medsys.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-04T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK topology & rotation cadence - MedSys private deployment

Thanks David — additional security clarifications and concrete asks from our side:

- Operator & custody model:
  * Recommend split custody for import/unseal operations: at minimum two operators required (operator A initiates, operator B completes). Use hardware-backed signing for approvals where available.
  * Ephemeral operator tokens should be minted by a centralized control plane (short TTL < 15 minutes) and bound to an operator's MFA session.

- Quorum / ceremony cadence:
  * For HSMs that support threshold unseal, document the minimum threshold and enforce via policy.
  * Rotation ceremonies: propose monthly key rolling for symmetric data keys and quarterly for root-wrapping keys. For high-risk workloads we can accelerate to bi-weekly for derived tokens.

- Audit & evidence format:
  * Import receipts (signed by HSM) + attestation logs (timestamped, hash-signed).
  * Telemetry watermarking: each rotation event should include a rotation-id and a signed digest that is pushed to your SIEM and Redwood Console. This allows correlating usage with rotation windows.

- Emergency flows (break-glass) and minimal-downtime revoke:
  * Break-glass should require an out-of-band approval (phone+email) and a short grace TTL for operator tokens.
  * Revoke path: prepare a quarantine policy that marks any newly-issued wrapped keys as invalid; route traffic to a degraded fallback model that uses a cached (rotated) wrapping key only for read-only calls until services are patched.

Attachments: per Rana's note, I reviewed medsys-encryption-requirements.pdf and added a light topology sketch (proposed-kms-topology-diagram.svg).

Monica — please draft a 60-day operational plan that includes: week-by-week ceremony rehearsals, attestation verification steps, and a replayable audit artifact that we will hand to MedSys for their SOC 2 reviewers.

Rana — for the workshop, we prefer 2026-04-07 09:30–11:00 PT. If that works we will circulate a pre-read and a short checklist of items to bring (HSM vendor model, network ACLs, sample SIEM endpoints).

Kimberly Park
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Kim/ David —

Thanks for the detailed recommendations. 2026-04-07 09:30 PT works for the workshop — please send the calendar invite and the pre-read. A couple of quick clarifications before the call:

1) HSM vendor: we will be using SafeHaven HSM v3.2 (on-prem appliances in our tenant). They support threshold unseal and import receipts but require a proprietary import token.
2) SIEM endpoint: splunk-collector.medsys.internal (TLS 1.3 only). We will only accept telemetry that has been redacted of any key material; signed digests are fine.
3) For the break-glass policy, our compliance team insists that revocation be auditable and require at least two approvers outside the SRE on-call.

I'll upload the vendor import token procedure and the SOC scoping doc to the Drive link you shared. Please put together a short template for the rotation artifact (JSON + signed digest) that our auditors can validate.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — see you at the workshop.

Best,
Rana
